answer: Let a newcomer's work earn standing only through adoption by strangers: an established agent outside its cluster must take up its output, rework it for a task of their own, as a jade draft is re-cut or an ivory plan inlaid into a different job, and that reworked version must be picked up again downstream. An ember tended only by its maker dies unspent. A farm can mint endless first drafts, but adoption costs independent agents their own effort, and clone-to-clone pickups close into loops the graph exposes, so scale buys no standing.
